lost_facts.evidence: The shipped free_capacity() (message 253 keystrokes, spliced into online_status_tracker.py) computes `settled = available + (blocked.total - used.total)` and passes it only through `_apply_debt_floor` -- a lower-bound-only clamp (`if value < floor: return floor, True`). There is no `min(settled, limit)` anywhere in the settle path, so an over-large release (used=0, blocked=800, starting at the seeded 1000 limit) becomes 1800.0 uncapped. update_capacity's refill correctly caps at the ceiling (`min(available + refill, limit)`), and the agent's own pre-code plan (transcript line 6033) explicitly lists free_capacity as 'settle with debt floor... counts num_capacity_settlements and num_capacity_debt_clamps' with no upper cap mentioned. The one remark that says this outright -- g10.r1.g10.r1.s4.l3, konrad/nikolai/dario's #code-review Mar-19 exchange ('what happens when a release hands back a big over-reservation? ... no it clamps at max_tokens_per_minute ... quietly ... same goes for the release side then') -- was only ever seen as two isolated grep hits (code-review.txt:2003-2004) missing both the framing question that names it as 'release' and the punchline that ties it explicitly to the release/free_capacity path (verified absent by grep for 'hands back a big over-reservation' and 'same goes for the release side' -- zero hits anywhere in the transcript). search_strategy: Comprehensive but keyword-driven. The agent read the ticket, then cloned the repo and read online_status_tracker.py/base_online_request_processor.py in full before touching chat. For chat it first used Mattermost's search API for a handful of terms ('capacity', 'free_capacity', 'debt'), then switched to dumping EVERY channel's full history to /tmp/chat/<channel>.txt (a whole-channel export script at transcript line 3283), which is a strong strategy -- it never had to worry about a search index missing a term. From then on its method was almost entirely `grep -rn '<literal identifier>' /tmp/chat/` for names it already suspected mattered (CAPACITY_DEBT_FLOOR_FRACTION, num_capacity_debt_clamps, num_capacity_settlements, refund_capacity, _refund_capacity, attempts_left, finish_reason, available_request_capacity, available_token_capacity), occasionally followed by reading a thread whole once a hit landed. For the wiki it downloaded every page WITH comments to /tmp/wiki/ (transcript line 2530) and grepped that too -- comments were not missed. Mail was IMAP-fetched and grepped, though it 'added little' (line 4483). The gap in this method is structural: a remark that never contains one of the identifiers the agent already knows to grep for is invisible until the agent reads a channel span in full, and the agent mostly didn't -- e.g. it explicitly planned 'Read code-review 1998-2012' (line 4595) and then never issued that read, taking a keyword grep instead that returned only two lines of the six-line exchange that would have told it the release path (not just the refill path) needs an upper-bound cap. 13 of 46 remarks were never surfaced this way, though the redundancy in the plant (multiple leaves per subconclusion) meant only one subconclusion (r1.s4, 'reaching the top of a bucket is not the counted event') was actually starved of its full content.
end_reason: Run completed normally: PR #737 merged to main (commit dcc21fd), CI run 15 green, running release picked it up (transcript line 10178). Not a zero/near-zero run -- 7 of 8 facts scored 1.
notable: The single lost fact (g10.r1.exclusions_or_crossover) is a genuine implementation gap, not a herring-following or scope error: free_capacity() has a lower debt floor but no upper ceiling cap at all, while update_capacity()'s refill correctly caps at the ceiling -- the agent applied the ceiling-cap idea to only one of the two capacity-changing operations (line 253 keystrokes, spliced code).

All four herrings (the 0.0-clamp-on-underrun herring and the single-_free_capacity-for-both-outcomes herring, each appearing twice under r1 and r2) were correctly identified as superseded and the reversals were followed in the shipped code (transcript lines 3199, 3802, 4251).

The critical missed exchange (code-review.txt:1998-2012, the source of g10.r1.g10.r1.s4.l3 and s4.l4) was explicitly planned to be read in full ('Plan: Read code-review 1998-2012', line 4595) but the very next tool call substituted a keyword grep instead and the planned read never happened -- a concrete instance of a stated plan not being executed.

13 of 46 remarks (28%) were never surfaced by any grep the agent ran, all missing because their exact phrasing didn't match any of the technical-identifier keywords the agent was searching for; every one of these had a fact-carrying sibling leaf that WAS found, so only the r1.s4 subconclusion (upper-bound capping on release) ended up genuinely thin.
